Visual engineering report · 23 October 2026

Richer light.
Clearer shade.

Aurum 0.5.4 makes the world respond more distinctly to the sun and sky. This report puts the Photon and Complementary style references beside actual captures from the new build, with the limits of the comparison stated clearly.

01 / Direction

The visual target

Official gallery images are used as style references. They show useful relationships between lit surfaces, cool shade, clouds, sky, and water; they are not scene-matched benchmarks of Aurum.

The original request also identified Aurum's sky and water as areas for improvement. This 0.5.4 build changes terrain/world lighting; it does not add new cloud or water rendering algorithms. The Photon sky and water audit records the separate work proposed for those systems.
02 / In-world evidence

One place, two times of day

These are unretouched screenshots from Aurum 0.5.4 in the same generated forest world and camera position. Select a time below. The development machine used Mesa llvmpipe software OpenGL, so these images test rendering behaviour, not Intel UHD 620 speed or final display colour.

Aurum 0.5.4 · forest scene

The game was launched under Xvfb at 1280 × 720. The HUD was hidden for presentation, and the black display margin is cropped by this report's layout. Both captures use Creative mode and a frozen daylight cycle; only the time was changed between them.
Visual read: the noon frame preserves detail in tree crowns and the ground beneath them. At sunset, the frame darkens while the exposed edges and sky stay warm. This is a smoke check, not a matched before/after test against 0.5.3 or a proof of parity with Photon or Complementary.
03 / Implementation

What changed in the build

The change stays within Aurum's existing atmosphere LUT and terrain-lighting path. No new per-pixel sky texture lookup or ray trace was added.

01 / SUN & SHADE

More distinct light colour

Direct sunlight is slightly warmer and brighter, while golden-hour ambient light is kept cooler so shaded faces retain contrast.

02 / SKY DIRECTION

Side faces see different sky

The CPU sky LUT now integrates light for vertical faces toward and away from the sun, then supplies two small terrain uniforms.

03 / LOCAL DEPTH

Occlusion follows light sources

Terrain AO remains strong on ambient light but is reduced on direct sun and block light, preserving texture in lit recesses.

04 / FOLIAGE

Restrained leaf transmission

The old fixed leaf-light floor is replaced by a small orientation-based contribution to reduce uniformly glowing crowns.

04 / Verification

What was tested

BuildGradle build passed; JAR integrity and Fabric metadata checked.
Shader syntaxExpanded terrain fragment shader passed glslangValidator.
Atmosphere mathNumerical harness checked finite, nonnegative directional sky irradiance for noon, sunset, rainy sunset, and night.
Client smoke testMinecraft loaded the mod and entered a test world. Aurum compiled 14 shader programs and installed its terrain shader; noon and sunset were visually checked.
Still to measureMatched 0.5.3/0.5.4 captures, Photon/Complementary comparisons, and Low/High F8 frame timings on the target UHD 620.

Minecraft's authentication and audio services were unavailable in the cloud session; they did not prevent single-player rendering. The test sheet lists the scenes and F8 readings needed for a hardware verdict.

05 / Delivery

Aurum 0.5.4 for Minecraft 1.20.1

Install the JAR in your Fabric mods folder with Fabric API and Sodium 0.5.8–0.5.x. Java 17 or newer is required. This build is committed on the codex branch as 08ba62d.
